threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still pause at the sound of the 'whoosh' when the Overground trains pass by. Locals just carry on chatting, like it's a background track.
Caught the N37 last night, two guys arguing over who saw the best live act at the Academy—drunken passion or a marketing ploy? Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was truly in Neukölln when the lady on my corner started offering homemade baklava right outside the Kiosk. That blend of cultures hits differently.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Kebab shop that serves a full menu of vegan options at 3 AM, catering to night owls and plant lovers alike.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You notice the locals rolling their eyes and automatically ducking under the BART turnstile. Tourists just stare, confused, at the delays.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today where the driver gave a woman her birthday cake back after she forgot it at the last stop. Just feels like classic SF kindness.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think 'poble' means village, but here it just means we have our own quirky vibe—it's not a tourist trap, it's home.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they keep asking for a 'bocadillo' when they really mean a 'sandwich'—only locals know the subtle shifts in lingo.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newcomer by their confused look when the 106 doesn’t show up, yet everyone else seems unfazed by the wait.
Heard a guy on the N35 last night claiming he was the 'London Tube Whisperer' — turns out he just knew a lot about bus driver routes and their favourite snacks.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a local Kiosk open at 2 AM, serving fresh currywurst and a side of gossip. That felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a hidden café with a pet pig wandering around while hipsters sip oat milk lattes. It's surreal but oddly charming.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they don’t flinch at the screech of a BART train braking hard. The tourists always look like they just saw a ghost.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading passengers with a ukulele in the 31, instantly made the cramped bus feel like a concert. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí and shops, but the best vibe is sipping vermut on a Sunday in a quiet plaça, just watching life unfold.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still look at the metro map like it’s a puzzle, while locals confidently swipe in without a glance.
